codeReviewFindings.quote:
+  order.refundedCents += amountCents;
+  writeLedgerEntry({ orderId: order.id, amountCents, feeCents });

probes.guard: Same as correctness #1: complete function body visible, no try/catch, no transaction, no compensating decrement; parent call site unwrapped. Two sub-claims are not supported by the diff, however — `writeLedgerEntry`'s result is never awaited or assigned, so the "async and rejects" path would not even propagate as written, and nothing in the diff shows the order being persisted at all (applyRefund mutates an in-memory object and returns).

codeReviewFindings.correctedWording: The core defect is confirmed, but the claim overreaches on three points and should read: `order.refundedCents += amountCents` mutates the in-memory order before `writeLedgerEntry` is called; if the ledger write throws, the order object carries a refund with no ledger entry and nothing unwinds it. Drop "(presumably) persists" — no persistence call appears anywhere in the fully-shown function. Drop "is async and rejects" — the call's result is neither awaited nor returned, so a rejection would surface as an unhandled rejection rather than as the ordering failure described. Drop "a retried request could double-refund" — no retry or idempotency machinery is visible in the diff to support it. Citation: the openable anchor is `src/evals/fixtures/code-review-citations.ts:136-137`; `src/billing/refund.ts` has 48 lines and does not exist on disk.
